post.body_html:
Appco × Rightbrain

Automating candidate verification so recruiters can focus on placing people, not chasing paperwork.

Manual checks in high-volume placement firms cause bottlenecks

Every candidate placed needs to pass verification before they start: ID checks, right-to-work documentation, and certifications. For a temp recruitment agency placing dozens of candidates a week, that is a large amount of repetitive checking, cross-referencing, and chasing.

Onboarding coordinators were spending most of their time in a loop: check what has been submitted, identify what is missing, follow up with the candidate, wait, and check again. Conducting 400 checks per month, more than 5,000 a year, was not complex work, but it was time-consuming, and it sat entirely on a human’s plate.

The knock-on effect was direct. Candidates sitting in the verification queue were not starting. Placements were delayed. Revenue that should have been landing was waiting on someone to manually move a document through a checklist. At volume, this creates a huge bottleneck.

The problem was not a lack of process. There was a clear checklist. The problem was that executing it required a lot of human intervention, where 80–90% could be automated.

Verification that runs itself

When a candidate is confirmed for placement, the Rightbrain-powered pipeline initiates automatically. The agent works through the verification checklist, tracks what has been submitted, follows up on gaps, and compiles the completed pack. The coordinator steps in at the end to review and approve, not at every step along the way. That frees up their time to work on more complex cases.

The verification pipeline

Candidate confirmed → verified onboarding pack

When a candidate is confirmed for placement, their details enter the onboarding workflow automatically. The Rightbrain agent initiates the verification checklist: what documents are required, what checks need to be completed, and what is already on file from previous placements or prior submissions.

As documents come in, the agent cross-references each one against requirements — checking for expiry dates, inconsistencies, missing fields, and compliance gaps. Anything that does not pass is flagged immediately, with an automated follow-up sent directly to the candidate detailing exactly what is needed.

The agent tracks the status of every open item across every candidate in the pipeline simultaneously. Nothing waits in a queue because someone has not had time to review it.

Once all checks pass, the agent compiles a verified onboarding pack and routes it to the coordinator for final sign-off. The human reviews a completed file, not a half-finished checklist.

The coordinator’s role shifts from manually pushing the process through to overseeing it and signing off on the outcome — acting as a higher-level supervisor. The agent handles chasing, checking, and compiling. The human makes the final call.

What changed

Coordinators now have time to focus on more complex tasks

  • Coordinators are no longer the bottleneck. The repetitive loop of check, chase, wait, and check again is handled by the agent. Their time goes to the exceptions that need human judgement: a reference that does not add up, a candidate with unusual circumstances, or a compliance edge case that needs a decision.
  • Every candidate goes through the same checks every time. There is no variation based on who is handling the file or how busy the team is. Compliance coverage is consistent at scale.
  • Candidates are onboarded faster. Nothing sits in a queue waiting for a manual review. Follow-ups go out immediately when something is missing, not when someone gets around to noticing.
  • Placements start sooner. The time between “candidate accepted” and “candidate starts” is shorter because verification no longer depends on coordinator availability.
  • The pipeline scales without adding headcount. Doubling placement volume does not mean doubling the onboarding team. The agent handles the increase; coordinator capacity stays focused on quality and exceptions.

We spend a huge amount of time on calls. There’s so much good data in them, but it was always in an unstructured format. This takes that unstructured data and turns it into part of our core workflows.

Mike Lush
Appco Innovation and Data Operations Lead

Who this is for

Any recruitment business where the time between “candidate accepted” and “candidate starts” is longer than it should be

This workflow applies to any business placing candidates at volume, where manual verification creates significant bottlenecks.

It is particularly effective where compliance requirements are consistent across placements: the same checks, the same documents, and the same standards applied to every candidate. When the process is defined but the execution is manual, there is a strong case for automation.

The workflow runs inside the tools the team already uses. There is no new platform to manage and no new login for coordinators to remember. The agent operates in the background, surfacing only what needs a human decision.
